I'm using the executing-plans skill to implement this plan.

You asked me to run it directly in this session, so I'm not switching to subagent-driven-development. Tasks 1-3 are already complete in `.sdd/9-kkiln-log/progress.md`, so I resume at Task 4.

**Before any edit**

I haven't opened Task 4's brief, so I can't write its file changes yet. Any `<edit>` block now would be invented. First I confirm where I am, then read the brief:

<command>git status --short && git branch --show-current && git rev-parse --short HEAD</command>

This should show a clean tree on `feat/kiln-log` at `e2a64f0`. If it doesn't, I stop and ask. I'm on a feature branch, so I don't need consent to work on the base branch, and I don't need to record a start commit.

<command>uv run pytest -q tests/test_firing.py tests/test_glaze.py tests/test_cone.py</command>

This should give 13 passed (4 + 6 + 3), a baseline before I touch anything.

<command>sed -n '/Task 4/,/Task 5/p' specs/plans/9-kiln-log.md</command>

This is Task 4's brief, "Cooling curve export". I also re-read the plan header for a `Spec:` line, a `## Review Focus` section and a `Roadmap:` line, since the later steps depend on them.

**Then, in order**

1. Review the plan critically. If Task 4's brief has gaps or conflicts with Tasks 1-3 (for example, it needs a cone-to-temperature interface that Task 3 doesn't expose), I raise them with you before starting. Otherwise I create todos for Tasks 4-6.
2. Execute Task 4: mark it in progress, follow each step exactly, run the verification the plan names, mark it complete, and append a `Task 4: complete (commits …, tests: …)` line to `progress.md`. I repeat this for Tasks 5 and 6.
3. If a test fails repeatedly, an instruction is unclear or there's a blocker, I stop and ask rather than guess.
4. After Task 6 is verified, I run the whole-plan review. I compute `BASE=$(git merge-base <base-branch> HEAD)` once, then launch the code-reviewer (opus, using `requesting-code-review/code-reviewer.md`, with the plan, spec path and Review Focus word for word) and the Codex review (`--base <BASE>`) in the same message. I touch nothing until both return.
5. I merge the two findings lists and work them with receiving-code-review. I fix what holds up, re-run the plan's tests and commit the fixes.
6. I run the plan-completion protocol from writing-plans: resolve-before-defer gate, plan markup, deferred items, then retire the plan and, if applicable, its spec.
7. I announce "I'm using the finishing-a-development-branch skill to complete this work" and follow it. If the plan header has a `Roadmap:` line, I end with the matching handoff message and don't start the next stage.

**Message to you**

> Resuming `specs/plans/9-kiln-log.md` on `feat/kiln-log`. Tasks 1-3 are done per `progress.md` (13 tests passing across firing, glaze and cone). I'm running the rest directly here, as you asked. I'm confirming the clean tree and the baseline tests, then opening Task 4 (cooling curve export). I'll flag any gaps in the brief before I change anything. Otherwise I'll work through Tasks 4-6, then run the whole-branch review (code-reviewer plus Codex) before closing out the plan.
